PURPOSE We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of 11C-choline PET/CT for the detection of lymph node metastases from prostate cancer in patients with biochemical recurrence. MATERIAL

the addition of 18F-choline PET/CT imaging to conventional imaging in the management of prostate cancer patients who are at high risk of recurrence and who have a single positive lymph node on conventional imaging may improve patient management by avoiding unnecessary treatment in some patients and by guiding treatment in others.
the [11C]Choline PET/CT scan is useful for guiding lesion-targeted therapies in men with recurrent prostate cancer localized to a single pelvic or retroperitoneal lymph node on conventional imaging.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of [11C]-choline PET/ CT to guide lesion-targeted salvage therapy in men with prostate cancer recurrence limited to a single lymphnode at imaging.
the development and validation of a novel method for the detection and characterization of the prostate cancer recurrence.
the development of a new approach for the detection of prostate cancer recurrence in patients with a solitary lymph node metastasis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that [11C]Choline PET/CT is useful in guiding lesion-targetted salvage therapies in patients who have prostate cancer recurrence that is localized to one lymph node at imaging.
we have demonstrated that [11C] choline PET/CT can be a very useful tool in the management of patients with recurrent PCa.

we have shown that [11C] choline PET/CT can be used to guide lesion-targeted salvage therapy (LT-ST) in patients with prostate-specific antigen (PSA) recurrence and a single lymph node lesion at imaging, with a high likelihood of pathologic confirmation of the lesion and a low risk of pathologic confirmation at other sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, when a patient with prostate cancer has a solitary lymph node lesion that is positive on imaging, the use of a targeted PET/CT agent such as [11C] choline can be a valuable tool in guiding treatment decisions.
the use of PET imaging in guiding salvage therapies is not a panacea, but rather an important tool in the armamentarium of the treating physician.
[11C] choline PET/CT is a useful tool in guiding the management of prostate cancer patients with biochemical recurrence and lymph node metastases.
